entries.problem_observed: A 10-shot, 50-second Agnes comedy assembled successfully but the lead's face, body, wardrobe and pendant drifted; Chinese name text could not be trusted as a generated in-scene control.
entries.minimum_mechanism: Separate renderer output from identity recognition. Preserve a hash-bound visual reference, use a local postproduction identity anchor/name layer when the user requests unmistakable naming, and treat it as a delivery aid rather than proof of identity-locked video.
entries.local_fit: Directly updates the role of Agnes: real short-clip production is viable, but character-continuous mainline drama still requires a separately evidenced reference-controlled renderer or a consciously local postproduction anchor.
not_adopted: No claim that Agnes accepts reference images, locks identity, or reliably renders Chinese text.
No user-supplied image or rendered media is copied into the public-learning ledger or Git sync.
entries.next_verification: Run an isolated, fictional/generated-character static-keyframe A/B only when an eligible local renderer has been installed and its license and resource fit are verified.

entries.problem_observed: A one-shot natural-language prompt loses visual reference and quality constraints before rendering.
entries.minimum_mechanism: Before generation, classify missing inputs as knowledge, reference, or quality constraints; then create a prompt-reference program that binds evidence, asset references and checkable requirements to the renderer.
entries.local_fit: Directly reinforces the episode_003 character/scene/prop contract and pre-generation quality gate.
not_adopted: No training, RL, weight distillation or privileged teacher runtime is adopted.
No external content body, credentials or private data is imported.
entries.next_verification: Create one renderer-agnostic prompt-reference program for episode_003, then test whether the chosen video provider accepts bound reference images; do not claim reference-driven video before that evidence exists.

entries.license_or_availability: Public documentation; FFmpeg project licensing varies by build (LGPL/GPL configuration must be checked before redistribution).
entries.problem_observed: Short-clip recovery and assembly can hide timestamp discontinuities or inaccurate cut boundaries, making a playable file look complete while temporal handoff is wrong.
entries.minimum_mechanism: Use FFmpeg concat/segment contracts as an audit aid: keep segment stream parameters compatible, preserve explicit segment ordering, and treat timestamp/seek-boundary behavior as evidence to validate after resume or re-assembly.
entries.local_fit: Adds a renderer-agnostic post-assembly check for the existing short-clip workflow; it complements, but does not replace, per-shot continuity audits and SHA-256 media receipts.
limitations: Concat does not repair identity, wardrobe, prop or spatial drift.
Segment accuracy depends on keyframes and constant-frame-rate assumptions; a successful mux is not proof of narrative continuity.
No FFmpeg binary, filter graph or second scheduler is adopted by this ledger entry.
not_adopted: No production route change or new runtime service.
No claim that timestamp checks prove provider-side video correctness.
entries.next_verification: On an existing local, fictional clip set, compare pre/post-resume concat output for stream parameters, duration, monotonic timestamps and SHA-256; record only measurable failures or improvements.

entries.license_or_availability: BSD-3-Clause (repository metadata verified 2026-09-05); public source and documentation.
entries.problem_observed: When a short drama is assembled from many generated clips, accidental hard cuts, duplicate frames or overlong holds can be mistaken for intentional scene transitions and weaken continuity review.
entries.minimum_mechanism: Run scene-boundary detection as a read-only audit signal to enumerate likely cuts and compare them with the declared shot contract; use the result to target human/frame-level review rather than auto-accepting edits.
entries.local_fit: Provides a lightweight audit candidate for episode-level pacing and boundary checks already present in research artifacts; it does not become a required production dependency.
limitations: Cut detection is heuristic and can miss semantic continuity failures or flag intentional motion/lighting changes.
Repository activity and model behavior can drift; re-check version and license before reuse.
No copied model weights, media, private data or provider control plane is imported.
not_adopted: No automatic scene rewriting or second pipeline.
No claim that boundary detection validates character identity, Chinese text, dialogue or causal plot logic.
entries.next_verification: Run one isolated comparison on an existing local episode assembly: declared shot boundaries vs detector output, measuring false positives/negatives before deciding whether to retain the audit hook.
